claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hi! I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and would like to know if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who's 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information!

To continue assessing your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I have a few more questions:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you!

**Is Alex in full-time education or training, or are they currently not in education?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 13, so still in school - just doing regular secondary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying.

Now I need to ask about your own circumstances:

**Are you currently living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not living in the UK at the moment. I'm currently abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

Since you're currently living abroad, I need to ask a few more questions:

**Are you living abroad temporarily or is this a permanent move? And could you tell me which country you're currently living in?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living abroad - it's not just a temporary thing, I've moved here. I'm currently in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since you've permanently moved abroad to Spain, I have a couple more questions:

**Do you work for the UK government in any capacity (for example, as a civil servant, diplomat, or member of the armed forces posted overseas)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't work for the UK government or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me also check the information about living abroad and Crown servants to be thorough:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information I've gathered, I now have enough to make an eligibility determination. Let me summarise:

- You have one child, Alex, aged 13, who lives with you
- You have permanently moved to Spain
- You do not work for the UK government

According to the UK government rules, to qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to **live in the UK**. There are exceptions for people who work for the UK government abroad (Crown servants), but since you've confirmed you don't work for the UK government, this exception doesn't apply to you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 13):** While Alex meets the age requirement (under 16) and lives with you, the fundamental eligibility requirement for Child Benefit is that **you must live in the UK**. Since you have permanently moved to Spain and do not work for the UK government (which would be an exception to this rule), you do not qualify.

The rules do allow some people living abroad to claim Child Benefit, but this is generally limited to Crown servants (such as UK government employees, diplomats, or armed forces members posted overseas). Since this doesn't apply to your situation, you would not be eligible.

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you return to live in the UK—you may wish to apply at that time.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. Is there anything else I can help you with?
